prompt: Two students, P and Q, of identical mass climb the same vertical flight of stairs. Student P runs up the stairs in 8.0 s, whereas student Q walks up the stairs in 16.0 s. Which statement correctly compares the work done against gravity and the average power developed by student P with that of student Q?
options: P does the same work as Q, and P develops twice the power of Q
P does twice as much work as Q, and P develops twice the power of Q
P does the same work as Q, and P develops half the power of Q
P does twice as much work as Q, and both develop the same power

answer.explanation: Both students have identical mass m and climb the same vertical height h, so work done against gravity W = mgh is identical. Student P takes half the time of student Q, so P develops P_power = W / 8.0 = 2 * (W / 16.0), which is twice the power.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 is correct. Work depends only on mgh (independent of time); power is inversely proportional to time.
Option 2 incorrectly assumes that moving faster requires more work against gravity.
Option 3 inverts the power relationship, claiming running develops less power.
hints: Work against gravity depends on mass, g, and vertical height: does it depend on time?
Power is work divided by time: who takes less time for the same work?
solution: Work done = mgh, identical for both students. Power = W / t. Since t_P = 0.5 t_Q, Power_P = 2 * Power_Q. Option A is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Emphasize the clear distinction between work done (independent of time) and power (rate of work done).
Since m and h are the same, work is identical.
Since P finishes in half the time, P's power is double Q's power.
